attribution.support_quote:
By leveraging the now
standard BERT pretrained model (Devlin et al.,
2019) and a dual-encoder architecture (Bromley
et al., 1994), we focus on developing the right
training scheme using a relatively small number
of question and passage pairs. Through a series
of careful ablation studies, our ﬁnal solution is
surprisingly simple: the embedding is optimized
for maximizing inner products of the question and
relevant passage vectors, with an objective compar-
ing all pairs of questions and passages in a batch.
Our Dense Passage Retriever (DPR) is exception-
ally strong.

attribution.support_quote:
The model takes as input the question, as well as
the support passages, and generates the answer.
More precisely, each retrieved passage and its title
are concatenated with the question, and processed
independently from other passages by the encoder.
We add special tokens question:, title: and
context: before the question, title and text of
each passage. Finally, the decoder performs atten-
1lucene.apache.org
2spacy.io
3github.com/facebookresearch/faiss
tion over the concatenation of the resulting repre-
sentations of all the retrieved passages. The model
thus performs evidence fusion in the decoder only,
and we refer to it as Fusion-in-Decoder.
By processing passages independently in the en-
coder, but jointly in the decoder, this method differs
from Min et al. (2020) and Lewis et al.

contribution of improving the retriever during pre-training.
Encoder or Retriever
We ﬁrst aim to determine whether
REALM pre-training improves the retriever or the encoder,
or both. To do so, we can reset the parameters of either
the retriever or the encoder to their baseline state before
REALM pre-training, and feed that into ﬁne-tuning. Reset-
ting both the retriever and encoder reduces the system to
our main baseline, ORQA. We ﬁnd that both the encoder
and retriever beneﬁt from REALM training separately, but
the best result requires both components acting in unison.

Encoder or Retriever
We ﬁrst aim to determine whether
REALM pre-training improves the retriever or the encoder,
or both. To do so, we can reset the parameters of either
the retriever or the encoder to their baseline state before
REALM pre-training, and feed that into ﬁne-tuning. Reset-

our main baseline, ORQA. We ﬁnd that both the encoder
and retriever beneﬁt from REALM training separately, but
the best result requires both components acting in unison.

claim_diagnostics.statement: 采用双编码器架构，并优化嵌入以最大化问题和相关段落向量的内积。
使用了Natural Questions、TREC、WebQuestions和TriviaQA等数据集。
DPR模型在四个数据集上优于之前的最佳结果，准确匹配率提高了1%到12%。
SQuAD数据集的问题缺乏上下文，因为问题是在看到段落后由注释者编写的。
该方法在编码器中独立处理段落，在解码器中联合处理，从而能够处理大量段落。
Fusion-in-Decoder方法在TriviaQA和NaturalQuestions基准测试上取得了新的SOTA结果。
该方法需要包含数十亿参数的模型，这使得查询和训练模型成本高昂。
REALM使用检索增强的语言模型预训练方法，通过优化语言模型的困惑度来训练检索器。
实验在NATURALQUESTIONS-OPEN、WEBQUESTIONS和CURATEDTREC三个开放问答基准数据集上进行。
在NQ开发集上，REALM在精确匹配和零样本检索召回@5上分别达到38.5和52.0。
REALM的性能在不同预训练语料库上有所差异，且需要进一步研究以确定其对编码器和检索器的具体贡献。
